# ADR-0006 The table set is a checked-in manifest, regenerated by a script

## Status

`built`. Taken in `fcdc305`.

## Decision

Dagster needs asset keys at definition time, but a zip's members are only known after download. So the member list for each source file is checked in as `PUBLOG_SOURCE_MANIFEST`. A script, `scripts/discover_manifest.py`, regenerates it by reading each zip's central directory over HTTP Range requests, which fetches a few KiB instead of the whole archive.

At run time staging compares the manifest with the real archive. It warns when a declared member is missing, and when the archive holds a CSV the manifest does not declare.

## Why

The commit message gives the key-time constraint above. It says a stale entry should degrade loudly, not silently.

## Consequences

A new member in the source has no asset until someone runs the script and commits the result. Until then the member is not staged and the warning is the only sign. A declared member missing from the archive makes its table asset fail.

The counts in the manifest tests come from a production run described in the test docstring. The run itself is not in the repo.
